description:
A hydrologist has water quality monitoring station data in a CSV file and needs to create Voronoi (Thiessen) polygons to define each station's coverage zone.

The CSV file is located at /home/ga/GIS_Data/bay_area_water_stations.csv and contains 8 USGS-based monitoring stations in the San Francisco Bay Area with columns: station_id, station_name, longitude, latitude, ph, dissolved_oxygen_mg_l, temperature_c.

Perform the following steps:
1. Import the CSV file as a delimited text layer in QGIS (Layer > Add Layer > Add Delimited Text Layer). Set the X field to 'longitude', the Y field to 'latitude', and the CRS to EPSG:4326 (WGS 84).
2. Verify that 8 point features appear on the map canvas.
3. Generate Voronoi polygons from the imported point layer using Vector > Geometry Tools > Voronoi Polygons.
4. Export the resulting Voronoi polygon layer as a GeoJSON file to: /home/ga/GIS_Data/exports/voronoi_zones.geojson

The exported GeoJSON should contain the Voronoi polygons with the original station attributes (station_name, ph, dissolved_oxygen_mg_l, etc.) preserved in each polygon's properties.
